title: parseBody has no body size limit — memory exhaustion on large payloads
detail: api/_shared/parseBody.js accumulates the entire request body in a string before JSON-parsing. There is no maxBytes check. Vercel's platform-level 4.5MB limit is the only bound. Routes using parseBody (history, library, settings via checkout) can be fed large payloads within that limit without route-level rejection, wasting function memory and invocation time.
fix_hint: Add a maxBytes check: reject with 413 before accumulating more than ~64KB.

title: getSession loopback URL constructed from unvalidated x-forwarded-host header
detail: api/_shared/auth.js:38 builds the loopback URL as `${protocol}://${host}/api/auth/session` where host = req.headers['x-forwarded-host'] || req.headers.host. A crafted host header could redirect this internal fetch (which carries the caller's session cookies) to an arbitrary external host. On Vercel managed infrastructure x-forwarded-host is set by the platform and cannot be caller-controlled, so this is low severity in deployment but structurally unsafe for any non-Vercel deployment.
fix_hint: Validate host against TRUSTED_ORIGINS before using it in the loopback URL, or use a hardcoded base URL from an env var.

title: Master API key compared with === (not timing-safe)
detail: api/_shared/apiAuth.js:47 checks `if (master && key === master)`. String equality is not timing-safe — an attacker measuring response latency differences across many requests could theoretically enumerate the key character-by-character. Practical exploitation requires many precisely timed requests, but the master key is the highest-privilege credential in the system.
fix_hint: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(key), Buffer.from(master)) — both buffers must be equal length (pad/hash first to avoid length leak).

title: Rate limiter is fail-open — KV outage disables burst protection
detail: api/_shared/ratelimit.js:26 returns {ok:true} when incrWithTtl returns null (KV unavailable). This is intentional (paid searches must not fail on KV outage) but means a KV outage or an attacker-induced KV unavailability disables the burst cap. The credit ledger remains the durable quota, but burst throughput is uncapped.
fix_hint: Consider a in-process LRU fallback rate limiter when KV is unavailable. Or accept the risk (credits are the real quota).

title: API_KEY_PEPPER is optional — unpepped key hashes are offline brute-forceable on DB leak
detail: api/_shared/crypto.js:69 — `const pepper = process.env.API_KEY_PEPPER || ''`. If API_KEY_PEPPER is not set, all key hashes are SHA-256(key) with a known prefix (oc_live_). A DB leak + knowledge of the key format enables offline dictionary/brute-force attacks on the short random suffix (24 bytes = 32 base64url chars, but entropy is 192 bits — brute-force is not feasible). The real risk is that without a pepper, a DB dump alone is sufficient to test candidate keys without hitting the API.
fix_hint: Set API_KEY_PEPPER to a random 32-byte hex string in Vercel env and document it as required.

title: api/settings.js reads req.body directly instead of parseBody — inconsistent body handling
detail: api/settings.js:51 accesses `req.body ?? {}` directly (relying on Vercel's automatic body parsing) while all other POST routes use parseBody() for stream-based reading. This is inconsistent — if Vercel body parsing is ever disabled (e.g., per-route config), settings POST would silently receive undefined body.

title: vercel.json has no security headers — no CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options
detail: vercel.json contains only two rewrite rules and no `headers` block. There are no global HTTP security headers set: no Content-Security-Policy, no Strict-Transport-Security, no X-Frame-Options, no Referrer-Policy, no Permissions-Policy. The proxy route adds X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff per response but this is not applied globally. Without CSP, XSS in any page has full document access.
fix_hint: Add a `headers` block in vercel.json with at minimum: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff, X-Frame-Options:DENY, Referrer-Policy:strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a Content-Security-Policy appropriate for the SPA.

title: Keyed per-source routes (Europeana/DPLA/Smithsonian) are unauthenticated — quota drain risk
detail: api/search/europeana.js, dpla.js, smithsonian.js have no auth, no rate limit, and no credit charge. Any caller with network access to the Vercel function URLs can send unlimited queries, burning the project's Europeana/DPLA/Smithsonian API quota without any cost to themselves. These URLs are discoverable from the client adapter source code.
fix_hint: Add a simple origin/referer check or a lightweight auth token (e.g., require a valid session cookie, or check Origin against TRUSTED_ORIGINS). Rate-limiting via IP would also help.

title: BL SPARQL route injects query into SPARQL template with minimal sanitization
detail: api/search/bl.js:15 — `query.replace(/"/g, '')` is the only sanitization before the query string is interpolated into a SPARQL FILTER. This strips double quotes but does not prevent other SPARQL injection patterns (e.g. `#` comment injection, backslash sequences, FILTER bypass with `LCASE(STR('x')) || LCASE(STR(?title))`). Practical impact is limited to data manipulation in the results returned to the browser.
fix_hint: Use parameterized SPARQL via the Upstash or a SPARQL-safe encoding, or at minimum strip all non-alphanumeric characters from the query before injection.

title: Mexicana route passes resumptionToken from query param directly into OAI-PMH URL
detail: api/search/mexicana.js:51 — `encodeURIComponent(token)` is applied but the token value is otherwise unvalidated before being appended to the OAI-PMH URL. A crafted token could manipulate the OAI verb or inject additional query parameters if the OAI endpoint is lenient in parsing. The upstream (mexicana.cultura.gob.mx) would likely reject malformed tokens.
fix_hint: Validate that resumptionToken matches a known format (alphanumeric + limited punctuation) before using it.

title: Proxy route does not enforce https: scheme — HTTP downgrade not blocked
detail: api/proxy.js:61 checks only the hostname against the allowlist, not the URL scheme. A caller can pass `http://gallica.bnf.fr/...` and the proxy will forward in plaintext. The platform will likely upgrade to HTTPS for most hosts but the proxy itself provides no scheme enforcement.
fix_hint: Add `if (targetUrl.protocol !== 'https:') return new Response('Only HTTPS targets allowed', { status: 400 });` before the allowlist check.

title: Proxy follows redirects without re-validating the redirect destination hostname
detail: api/proxy.js:78 sets `redirect: 'follow'`. If an allowlisted upstream host issues an HTTP redirect to a non-allowlisted or internal host (e.g. 169.254.169.254 metadata endpoint, or an internal service), the proxy follows the redirect without re-checking the destination against ALLOWED_DOMAINS. This is a classic SSRF-via-redirect vector.
fix_hint: Set `redirect: 'manual'`, then check the Location header against ALLOWED_DOMAINS before following, or use `redirect: 'error'` and return a 302 to the client to follow directly.

title: Proxy 502 error body leaks upstream error.message
detail: api/proxy.js:103 returns `{ error: 'Proxy Execution Error', details: error.message }` where error.message can include the target URL, network error details, or internal host resolution information visible to the caller.
fix_hint: Log error.message server-side and return only a generic 'Upstream unreachable' message to the caller.

title: No per-user API key count limit — a user can mint unbounded keys
detail: api/keys.js:50-59 — POST creates a new key without checking how many the user already has. Each key still spends from the user's own credit pool, so the financial impact is self-limiting. The risk is that a large number of keys creates noise in the api_keys table and makes key management harder.
fix_hint: Reject POST when the user already has N (e.g. 10) non-revoked keys.

title: AUTH_SECRET env var not validated at startup — absent/weak secret allows session forgery
detail: api/auth/handler.js passes AUTH_SECRET from process.env to the Auth.js config without checking it is present or of sufficient length. If AUTH_SECRET is unset or empty, Auth.js v5 will reject it at runtime (throws on token signing), but there is no startup-time assertion that surfaces the misconfiguration early. A weak/known secret could allow session token forgery.
fix_hint: Add a startup check: `if (!process.env.AUTH_SECRET || process.env.AUTH_SECRET.length < 32) throw new Error('AUTH_SECRET must be at least 32 chars');`

title: Checkout baseUrl accepts any *.vercel.app origin for post-checkout redirects
detail: api/checkout.js:28 — `if (origin && (TRUSTED_ORIGINS.includes(origin) || origin.endsWith('.vercel.app'))) return origin;`. The `*.vercel.app` pattern accepts any Vercel preview deployment from any account, not just OpenCITE's own. A malicious actor could create a Vercel project at `evil.vercel.app`, craft a checkout request with `Origin: https://evil.vercel.app`, and redirect users there post-checkout.
fix_hint: Restrict the vercel.app check to a known project prefix: `origin.endsWith('-opencite.vercel.app') || origin.match(/^https:\/\/opencite.*\.vercel\.app$/)`.

title: Webhook silently no-ops when client_reference_id absent and stripe_customer_id has no DB match
detail: api/stripe/webhook.js:104 — resolveUserId returns null when neither client_reference_id nor a matching stripe_customer_id is found. The event is still claimed in processedEvent (no retry), but no credit/plan update occurs. This can happen if a customer was created in Stripe manually or if the DB reference was lost.
fix_hint: Log a structured warning when userId is null for a handled event type so it surfaces in Vercel logs.

title: Webhook trusts Stripe metadata for pack/plan attribution — safe only while STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is uncompromised
detail: api/stripe/webhook.js:117 uses obj.metadata.pack and obj.metadata.plan to determine what credits/plan to grant. Stripe metadata is only writable via the secret key, so this is safe in normal operation. If STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is compromised, an attacker could craft arbitrary checkout sessions with inflated pack/plan metadata.
fix_hint: Cross-validate pack/plan from metadata against CREDIT_PACKS/PLANS before granting — reject unknown values explicitly.
